transcript.text: The range skill just got some major changes in RuneScape Dragon Wilds, and in this video, I'll go over not only
what's been added, but also how to level the skill as quickly as possible, what unlocks you'll get along the way, and
the best gear for you to wear, no matter how far into the game you are. Starting off, I just wanted to go over
the skill tree and what you will be unlocking as you level up the range skill. Now, to start out, for each level
that you get in between different levels, you'll get a range stamina cost reduction. This makes it cheaper for you
to simply make your range attacks, so that way you don't have to wait for stamina as long. Next, at level three,
you'll be able to perform quick attacks, making your shots come out a little bit faster. Then, at level five, you'll
unlock the ability to craft an archery target, followed by level eight, where you get the trick shot ability, which
makes it so that when you fully draw your bow, if you release the shot at the perfect time, you'll do some bonus
damage. Up next is the range special actions, which there are three of, and I'll go over a little bit more later on.
Then, at level 12, you'll get the snare skill, which simply lets you place down a earth magic root, and when enemies
walk inside of it, they'll be rooted into the ground. It's important to note that this one can be used alongside
other skills, so it's worth getting ranged at least to 12, no matter what. Then, you have toxic behavior, which is
unlocked at level 15 and allows you to craft weapon poison, which, again, can be used with other skills, since you can
apply poison to different melee weapons, as well as craft poison arrows. Up next, at level 18, you'll gain access to
hunter sense, which allows you to see enemies through walls. It's probably worth noting here that we're expecting
this one to change over to the hunter skill when we eventually get it, but that's still several months away. Then,
you have your first tier of ammo recovery, which rewards you with a chance to recover arrows from the bodies
of any enemies that you take out. Moving on, we have make them bleed, which allows you to craft weapon barbs, which
can be, once again, used with melee weapons to cause bleed damage, or to craft barbed arrows to cause a bleed
effect rather than a poison effect. At level 25, you'll get spectral arrows, which when equipped allows your bow to
do some additional damage and penetrate your arrows through enemy targets. Then we have leg shot at level 28, which is
one of the newer skills that allows you to slow enemy combatants as long as you shoot them either in their legs or in
their lower third of their hip box. Moving on to level 30, we get the crossbow trick shot, which is one of the
highest DPS increases since it allows you to instantly reload your crossbow as long as you time the reload right. Think
Gears of War if you haven't done this before. At level 35, the crossbow becomes even more powerful as you'll get
enchanted crossbow bolts, which allow you to enchant your crossbows for some additional elemental effects. Then at
level 40, you get venomous trapper, which will cause the trap that you place on the ground to also apply a poison
debuff over time. Coming in at level 45, you've got fire starter, which will now let you craft fire oil, which lets you
make fire arrows so you can get both extra damage and a burn effect. We're almost there now with level 50, which
gives you greater ammo recovery, simply giving you an even higher chance to recover your arrows from the bodies of
slain enemies. Our second-to-last major skill comes in the form of lucky bolts, which increases the chance for your
enchanted crossbow bolts to trigger their magical effects. And finally at level 99, you unlock the ever
prestigious range skill cape, which when worn makes so all range attacks have a chance not to consume any stamina. Now,
let's go ahead and talk about the different bow types. You have the short bow, long bow, and crossbow, all coming
with their own unique special attacks, meaning they're better at different situations. The short bow will allow you
to step backwards and then fire a quick burst of three arrows in a straight line at your target. The long bow on the
other hand will give you a sniper shot where you can get on one knee and fire an extremely powerful shot doing some
massive damage to the target. And then finally, you have the crossbow and its special attack. What's unique about this
is that it is a one-handed weapon, but more importantly, when you use the special skill, it can apply effects from
your enchanted crossbow bolts, as well as having one of the highest single target damages that you can currently
have, at least for the ranged category. Now, I wanted to take a moment to go over some of the different leveling tips
for the actual range skill, starting off from the fresh character. In the beginning, when you're in Brimstone
Needle Valley, and you can either craft an ash shortbow from the crafting table, or travel to this cave here, windstep
across the gap, and chop down the thorny vines to find a recipe for the adventurer's longbow. Either of these
bows will honestly work completely fine, though, as they will get replaced pretty
darn soon as soon as you start to leave the starter zone. And both will do the job of getting you some early levels in
the skill. You'll also need to craft yourself some stone arrows and start farming cows and goblins in the area in
order to get the items you need for the recipes. The best place to farm mobs in this zone is either here at the goblin
camps to the east, or you can simply just go inside one of the vaults located at the north and south of the zone, and
defeat enemies inside of there. Once you farm enough cows to craft the leather ranged armor set, you will be ready to
head over to the fractured planes biome. It's important to note that all ranged armor sets give the exact same passive
bonus, just the higher level tiers provide you with more armor and more defensive stats. [music] The way the set
bonuses work is if you have one piece of ranged gear equipped, you get plus 40 to your stealth speed. [music] With two
pieces, you get minus 33% ranged stamina consumption. And with three equipped, you get an additional 25% damage to weak
points. Once you're in the fractured plane biome, though, you'll be able to complete the Heartstrings quest to
unlock your first masterwork weapon, which is the crystal bow. This weapon has a really nice AoE scattershot
ability, but my recommendation for the best ranged weapon to take on the first boss at least would either be the
hunter's stag bow which can be dropped from Garu hunters or the iron crossbow which you can simply make with some
iron. At range level 30 though, you will unlock one of my personal favorite perks which is the crossbow trick shot. This
gives you great mobility and damage if you're able to get the timing down. For armor, you can opt either for the
studded leather range set or head over to the blood blight swamp where you can unlock the wild archer range set from
the dragonkin effigies inside this vault here. Iron arrows are of course going to be the best arrows available to you at
this point in time, at least that you can craft, but bronze will work fine if you just happen to have tons of extra
bronze laying around. The storm touched Highlands though will be one of the best zones for you to farm some mobs for XP
before you take on the very first boss. And honestly, I wouldn't even suggest that you attempt the first boss with the
range skill unless you're at least at level 30 so that you can use the main attack style that you prefer before
taking it on, although it is definitely doable without doing this. Once you arrive at Fell Hollow, I would suggest
trying to unlock the dwarven shotgun crossbow by completing the even more restless ghost quest or the undead
rangers bow by interacting with the dragonkin effigy inside this vault. Otherwise, you can just craft the best
bow currently available to you until you're able to upgrade your hunter's stag bow, wild scout short bow, or
crystal bow at the mystic forge. Steel arrows will also be the best ammo available to you at least at this point
in time, so make sure that you're mining all the iron and coal that you come across since you're going to be needing
a lot of it. For farming spots, I like heading over to the village located here on the west side of Fell Hollow as the
zombies move extremely slow and there are places where you can sit on top of the runes and free fire down onto the
different mobs. You can also use the spectral arrows ability here to make your arrows pierce through all the mobs
granting you more XP. Additionally, make sure to take on each mini boss in the zone whenever they are up such as the
green dragon located here or the zogre located here. I'll go over a bit more about weak point damage later, but just
make sure to aim for the weak points as this will increase your damage output and therefore your XP. The best armor
available to you in this zone though will be the green dragonhide ranged armor or the ranger armor which is
purchased from death with soul fragments. After that is down and reach and in this zone you'll be able to
create a mithril tier crossbow or a maple bow depending on your preference as well as mithril arrows and bolts. I
suggest simply creating the best bow that you can from this tier until you can upgrade one of the vestiges or
masterwork weapons that I have previously mentioned. The snare ability will also be very useful in this zone as
there are multiple different rooms that have tons of different mobs such as knights or rats and you're able to
quickly throw down a snare and place them in there and then you'll kite them into it so you're able to lock them
down. I personally like to farm in the cathedral, the barracks, or the zogre beneath the grand hall. Before you take
on the final boss though, I suggest you have the best possible ranged armor which is either the blue dragonhide set
or the shadow set which is purchased from postie pete with infernal fragments. Next up will be the umbral
sand biome and here you'll gain access to you bows and adamant crossbows as well as adamant arrows and adamant
bolts. You are able to unlock the bow eldinis by completing the mapping the sands two quest line here pretty much as
soon as you enter the zone. This bow is extremely powerful and comes with a lunar rain special attack that pours
down water damage onto your enemies. This is particularly useful even more so in the umbral sands since all the kotar
are weak to water damage. So I highly recommend that you get it as soon as you are able to do so. If you do get stuck
on how to unlock it, I actually have a full video going over how to do this which goes over a full step-by-step
guide. My favorite place to farm in this zone, however, has to be either here in the middle of the zone where you can
just sit on top of the ruins and shoot down at the Kotar, as well as use your special attack, or here at the southwest
side of the zone where the Kalphite spawn frequently and are easy to take down from a distance. For armor, you can
choose between the red dragonhide set or the Kalphite carapace set, depending on
which one you think looks best. Finally, will be the scorned wilderness raid, which gives you access to rune tier
crossbows, arrows, and bolts, as well as magic bows. If you do not have an upgraded masterwork visage weapon
already, these will be your current highest damage options. As you begin to clear the raid though, you will get
access to the black dragonhide set, which will be the best range set currently available. Once you beat
Kerapac, however, you will have a chance to acquire the dragon crossbow from the queen slayer's reward pack, which is
currently the highest DPS crossbow in the game. Now, I just wanted to go over the best XP and damage buffs that you
should be using if you want to maximize your output with the range skill. And keep in mind that the higher damage you
do, the more XP you get. Firstly, you will of course always want to have the knowledge's nourishment buff going,
since this will give you an extra 10% XP no matter what it is you are doing. In order to get it, the easiest recipe for
you to craft would simply be the sweet veg ball. This pairs very well with a relentless infusion to decrease the
stamina cost of range attacks by 33%, allowing you to put out even more damage. For your rings and amulet,
however, I suggest using the unholy symbol and pairing it with either the inspiring amulet of range, the amulet of
glory, or the amulet of accuracy, depending on what level you're currently at and what scenario you're currently
in. Moving over to the animal buffs, you can choose to craft barbed, poison, or fire arrows once you unlock
>> effect on major bosses such as Velgar or Amaru, but do work on enemies such as
Zeugars and Dragons. As a reminder, the barbed arrows will cause a bleed effect, the poison arrows will cause the enemy
to take 5% of their maximum health as poison damage over the course of 6 seconds, and fire arrows will cause the
target to burn for 5% of their max health over those same 6 seconds. Overall, these are only going to be
useful a handful of times, and I would simply not go out way to spend the time crafting hundreds and hundreds of these
different arrows, especially when the damage return that you're getting just really isn't there. After that are the
enchanted crossbow bolts, which require the mining and collecting of different ores and gems in order to craft them,
and each one has a different elemental effect based on the type of bolt that you're currently creating. The enchanted
bronze and iron bolts are crafted with opals and jades, respectively, and have a chance to explode doing AoE damage.
The blue right bolts are crafted with jades and give you a chance to apply [music] a knockdown effect. The steel
bolts require topaz and provide a chance to recover health on impact. Next are the enchanted mythril bolts, which are
crafted with sapphires and have a chance to poison all nearby enemies. Then you have the enchanted adamantite bolts,
which will draw from your health to do extra damage. And finally, we finish things off with the enchanted rune bolt,
which is crafted with diamonds, and they give you a chance to pierce through enemies allowing you to deal extra
damage to multiple targets. When used correctly and enemies are lined up, you can deal a lot of extra damage with
these and therefore level the skill extremely quickly if you have access to it. Now, I did also want to give you
just a few quick tips when it comes to the range skill. The first being that you can actually use the scroll wheel if
you're on PC to quickly change between arrow types. I'm not sure what it is on console, but this can be extremely
useful when picking between the different status ammos available to you or conserving your best arrows against
the weaker mobs. Next is that the majority of mobs have a weak point with the majority of them being on the head.
This seems pretty obvious, but it's worth noting that you get a 0.5 x damage multiplier, so that you get more
experience when farming mobs rather than the normal 0.25 damage XP multiplier on regular hits. Finally, I wanted to
quickly go over some of the best end-game bows in my personal opinion, that is. As I mentioned earlier, the
wild scout shortbow and the crystal bow are both very good in terms of their attack speed, although the scout bow is
just slightly faster, so I tend to choose it over the crystal bow unless I need that extra AoE damage and don't
want to swap out to something else. Now, the hunter stag bow will have the highest raw damage in terms of long
bows, that is, >> [music] >> and it should be upgraded as soon as you get it. The bow of Eldenis is a nice
filler longbow, especially for taking on things like the fight caves where everything is weak to water damage. I
strongly, however, recommend the Dorgeshunn crossbow if you're going to use crossbows since the overall its
damage is extremely high and you only need a few undead bones to craft its special bone bolt ammunition. It's
important to note, however, that you can't use enchanted bolts for this crossbow, so I would probably just stick
to the rune crossbow if you want to use them, at least until you get extremely lucky and see the dragon crossbow drop
from Coldra if you're out for on farm. But, the range skill will only take you so far in RuneScape Dragon Wild, and so
if you want to hear me talk about the best way to level up the magic skill, consider checking out this video.
